events.title: CVE-2026-123039: Check Point Gateway Exploited Privilege Escalation Fixed in R82.20 Take 14
events.summary: A privilege escalation flaw in Check Point gateways, tracked as CVE-2026-123039, is reportedly being exploited to gain root access, deploy backdoors, and wipe ESXi systems. Check Point has addressed it in the R82.20 Take 14 release, and the record lists several related CVEs including a Linux kernel use-after-free issue and an Android remote code execution flaw patched by Telegram.

events.title: Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons
events.summary: Microsoft Research published threat research showing that an AI agent model can be turned into a sleeper agent by tampering with fewer than ten neurons to implant a small payload. The same research found such tampering is detectable, because frontier-level agent models can spot anomalous weight edits.
events.why_it_matters: This describes a low-cost, hard-to-spot tampering technique against agent models, with an exploit surface measured in single-digit neuron edits. For teams deploying agents, the key finding is that frontier agents can detect the anomalous weight edits, so model-level integrity checking becomes a practical defensive step. The record reports no in-the-wild exploitation or severity rating, so the immediate risk is unquantified.

events.why_it_matters: It highlights that dual-use system binaries become the payload when an agent is fed malicious instructions, so defenders may need structural controls and permission composition rather than regex blacklists, which the authors say miss structural evasions. Teams deploying agentic coding tools could use this framing to reassess how permissions are layered. The record cites no incidents or specific products affected.

events.summary: A research paper on arXiv introduces Latent Barrier Steering, a method for adding safety constraints to flow-matching-based generative planning systems. events.title: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization
events.summary: A research paper on arXiv proposes a new adversarial method ('Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks') that perturbs facial images to protect against identity cloning by personalized text-to-image diffusion models. It improves on prior defenses by using sparse perturbations instead of dense ones, avoiding visible distortion around facial features.
events.why_it_matters: Diffusion models can learn a person's identity from just a few reference photos, creating risk of unauthorized or misleading generated content. Proactive defenses like this one add adversarial perturbations to images before release to disrupt that identity acquisition. The paper suggests existing dense-perturbation methods can become visibly distorted, which has limited their practical use for image privacy.

events.title: BadMoE: Backdooring Mixture-of-Experts LLMs via Routing-Aware Triggers and Task-Underutilized Experts
events.summary: Researchers describe BadMoE, a proposed backdoor attack against Mixture-of-Experts language models, in which an adversary with white-box access manipulates routing-aware triggers and a small subset of experts so the model behaves maliciously on chosen tasks. The paper presents this as a model-supply-chain threat arising from MoE architectures' sparse expert activation.
events.why_it_matters: It highlights that MoE's modular, sparsely activated design creates a new attack surface: compromising a small share of experts could alter model behaviour. The threat model is white-box and supply-chain based, so it concerns parties who train, fine-tune or source model weights rather than end users of deployed APIs. No real-world exploitation is reported in the record.

events.title: MIRAGE: Misleading Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Black-box and Query-agnostic Poisoning Attacks
events.summary: Researchers have published a preprint describing MIRAGE, a multi-stage attack that poisons the document corpus used by retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. Unlike earlier poisoning research, it works in a strict black-box setting without needing access to the model internals or knowledge of the queries users will ask.
events.why_it_matters: The paper argues prior poisoning studies overestimated the barrier to real-world exploitation by assuming white-box access or known queries, so organisations relying on RAG may face a more practical threat than previously assumed. Defenders should treat the external knowledge sources feeding RAG systems as an attack surface that can be poisoned without insider access or foreknowledge of user questions.

events.title: RoCoMark: Robust Code Watermarking Against LLM-Based Functionality-Preserving Rewriting Attacks
events.summary: A research paper on arXiv proposes RoCoMark, a code watermarking method designed to survive LLM-based rewriting that preserves a program's functionality. The authors argue existing watermarks fail against such attacks because their training does not account for the global perturbations rewriting introduces.
events.why_it_matters: The paper addresses provenance: if LLM rewriting strips watermarks from AI-generated code, organisations lose the ability to trace where code came from. RoCoMark claims robustness against this class of attack, which is relevant to teams relying on watermarking for code provenance or licensing enforcement. As a preprint, its claims have not been independently validated.
